column1: # findings.tsv -- the readiness census's required findings matrix (PORTABILITY-MID-END-PORT-READINESS-CENSUS-1.md, section 15 of its brief): question, verdict, evidence (a results/ or programs/ file of audit/mid-end-port/readiness, or a source).
Are payload-bearing enums and exhaustive matches sufficient?
column3: recursive typed payloads, structural ==, exhaustive checking; costs: heap objects per payload value, match-bound values not scalar-replaced, impossible arms when one enum spans categories

column1: Can the actual mutual-recursion SCCs be expressed?
column3: mutual: unimplemented; 212 front-end procedures in cycles, largest 82 across 12 files; module imports acyclic; merged form allocates per request, function values excluded by contexts

column1: Which essential stdlib facilities remain missing?
column2: sort, String ordering, split/search/trim, format, struct update, typed empty collections, mutable element places
column3: each written by hand in the probe; nested collections quadratic

column1: Are ordinary collections and error effects adequate?
column3: flat tables and MutableMap places work; worklist index after a push unproven; no internal-failure convention

column1: Does a port-sized frontend program compile economically?
column3: 55,174 lines in 409 s, 5.1 GiB; linear to about 28,000 lines (6.5 ms per line)

column1: Are semantic instances still a blocker?
column3: 1,024 types accepted; total guard fails as HIR SEMANTIC LIMIT; walks flat per walk
memoizeViews copies the program per codegen instance; 16 passes 3.88 GiB, as in November

column1: Is generic native compilation adequate initially?
column3: 1.4-1.7x slower than specialized, about 3x faster than tuned Tcl; lowering fits

column1: Is HIR interchange a sufficient boundary?
column3: format 1 is a trusted same-front-end dict: 38 top-level tables, 17 node kinds, 12 registries, no schema

column1: Can shared semantic rules avoid duplication?
column3: the mid-end calls 14 core:: namespaces 27.9 million times over the call-graph corpus; type, value and decimal rules are the runtimes' too

column1: Can Botlish be integrated into the existing compiler process?
column2: yes on Linux and Windows, no on macOS; a subprocess everywhere
column3: native libraries load into tclsh (Tcl-extension probe); the C ABI carries text only

column1: Would a complete port materially speed up compilation?
column3: mid-end 76.9% of the gate: at most 4.3x (3.6x with a boundary crossing), realistically 1.8-2.2x with today's allocator, 2.8x allocation-free; the gate's structure fix alone saves more
needs mutual:, format 2, one statement of core rules, a differential harness; designed in section 17
